events.title: Birth of Augustine of Hippo
events.description: Augustine, the future bishop of Hippo Regius, was born in Thagaste in Roman North Africa. His writings, including Confessions and The City of God, became foundational texts of Western Christianity and philosophy.
events.significance: Augustine's theology shaped Christian doctrine and Western philosophical thought for over a millennium, influencing both Catholic and Protestant traditions.

events.title: St. Brice's Day Massacre
events.description: King Æthelred the Unready of England ordered the killing of Danes living in England. The order was carried out on this date, reportedly targeting Danish settlers across the kingdom.
events.significance: The massacre heightened Anglo-Danish tensions and is often cited as a factor leading to Sweyn Forkbeard's invasions and the eventual Danish conquest of England under Cnut.

events.title: U.S. Supreme Court Affirms Ruling Against Bus Segregation in Montgomery
events.description: The Supreme Court upheld a lower court decision in Browder v. Gayle, declaring Alabama's laws requiring segregated buses unconstitutional.
events.significance: The ruling effectively ended the Montgomery Bus Boycott's legal fight and was a major victory for the Civil Rights Movement, reinforcing the principle that segregation in public transportation was unlawful.

events.title: Eruption of Nevado del Ruiz and the Armero Tragedy
events.description: The Nevado del Ruiz volcano in Colombia erupted, melting glacial ice and triggering lahars that buried the town of Armero. Around 23,000 people were killed.
events.significance: One of the deadliest volcanic disasters of the 20th century, it exposed failures in hazard warning and evacuation and led to major improvements in volcanic risk monitoring and disaster preparedness.

events.title: Birth of Robert Louis Stevenson
events.description: Robert Louis Stevenson, the Scottish novelist and essayist, was born in Edinburgh. He later wrote Treasure Island, Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, and Kidnapped.
events.significance: Stevenson became one of the most widely read authors of the 19th century, and his works shaped adventure and Gothic fiction and remain widely adapted.
